bootstrap.resampled: source groups within each task, the mix weights applied afterwards

caption: Test split, run 0, n = 743, list prices 2026-10-12. Crosses are 95% intervals from 2,000 resamples of source groups within each task. Differences between policies are judged by the paired intervals in the tables, not by whether crosses overlap. Each cross is a frozen operating point: the threshold or cutoff the walk on dev chose before test was touched (routers/operating_points.json), evaluated here and not walked, labeled with its target. A step line joins A to the distinct frozen dials that route, strictest first, each evaluated on the split once; it is not a walk and shows no step the walk did not choose, so it is shorter than dev's, which shows every step the walk tried. E's, F's, G's and G+'s crosses mark their operating points; their step lines are in the router-started figure. haiku/free is one point with 95% intervals (it has no dial); haiku/Jev's and haiku/Sonnet's steps are joined by straight lines in linear cost from A (a frozen point that fell back to A has its cross at A). G's and G+'s costs include Jev's overhead per request, and E's and F's have none. A cascade's costs include every gate call it makes: the Jev gate's at $0.042 per million input tokens and the Sonnet gate's at list price.
note: 65% MBPP+, the task with the fewest test items (107), so its intervals are wider than the uniform mix's. MBPP+ is easier than typical coding traffic, so this mix likely overstates coding savings.

units.quality: share of items answered correctly, 0 to 1, mix-weighted in the headline figure
units.cost_per_1k: dollars per 1,000 requests, at list price, mix-weighted in the headline figure
units.configs: each config's quality and cost_per_1k: its value on test, the point plotted, with its percentile 95% interval (low, high), the cross's arm, and its standard error, the standard deviation over the resamples
units.envelope: the envelope's corners, cheapest first, joined by straight lines in linear cost
units.oracle: the oracle's corners: every item on its cheapest config, then the point after each upgrade, in the order taken, joined by straight lines in linear cost
units.oracle_max_quality: the quality at the oracle's last corner
units.routers: the routers on the chart, keyed by their name in the operating-points file; E is `rules`, the rules router
units.steps: A (threshold null) first, then each distinct frozen threshold that routes, from the highest down, each with its quality and cost_per_1k on test (mix-weighted in the headline figure), joined by straight lines in linear cost: the frozen points' dials evaluated on test, never a walk
units.operating_points: the policy's frozen operating points, keyed by quality target (the headline figure's panel, one mix) or by mix and then quality target (the per-task figure): the dials the operating-points file holds, evaluated on test, whose quality and cost_per_1k are each its value on test, the point plotted, with its percentile 95% interval (low, high), the cross's arm, and its standard error, the standard deviation over the resamples
units.threshold: the frozen point's threshold, null for a fallback to A
units.fell_back: the operating-points file's flag: the point is A itself (no router call, no overhead, captured fraction 0)
units.target: the quality target on test: its share of A's quality under the mix
units.captured: the point's captured fraction of the oracle's savings at its target (§7), with its percentile 95% interval over every resample (null being n/a), and met, the share of resamples in which it meets the target
units.routing: the share of requests answered by each config, weighted like quality and cost
units.matched_cost: the envelope's quality at the point's cost and the point's paired quality difference from it, with its percentile 95% interval (low, high; null being n/a), and unread (Amendment A9, items 12 and 15)
units.label: the router's name on the chart
units.operating_points_file: the file holding the router's section: the frozen points and the walk that chose them
units.operating_points_sha256: the sha256 of the router's section of the operating-points file, written with sorted keys
units.mcnemar: McNemar's test of the row against A within the task: b, the items only the row gets right; c, the items only A gets right; p, exact and two-sided, descriptive only. Null (shown as —) for a point that falls back to A
units.mcnemar_vs_A: the same for each fixed config against A; A's own row is null
units.savings_vs_A: A's cost per 1k less the config's, the oracle's or the point's (per_1k), and that as a share of A's (share)
units.difference_from_A: quality less A's, paired: the same resamples weigh both; its standard_error is the safety margin
units.failed_by_every_config: the test items no config gets right
units.targets: each quality target, keyed by its share of A's (opus's) quality under the mix: its quality, the oracle's cost there (null: infeasible), savings against A and routing mix, and the envelope's cost there and captured fraction

cascade_units.cascades: the 15 cascades, keyed by section key: label, start (the pure cascades start at haiku, the others at a router), gate, the operating-points file that holds the section and the sha256 of the section
cascade_units.panel_cascades: a panel's `cascades`: per cascade its label, gate and steps from A, then each distinct frozen dial that routes, strictest first, with its quality and cost_per_1k on test, joined by straight lines in linear cost
cascade_units.point: the free-checks-only cascade's one step as a point with a cross: its quality and cost_per_1k on test, each its value with its percentile 95% interval (low, high) and standard error; the cascade has no dial
cascade_units.operating_points: the frozen points' rows, keyed by quality target: threshold (the router's), cutoff (the gate's), fell_back, quality and cost_per_1k with intervals, difference from A, savings against A, captured fraction, routing mix, escalation rate and the matched-cost comparison
cascade_units.routed_panels: the router-started figure's panels, one per mix: A, the envelope's corners, the targets, and per router four lines on the router's frozen thresholds: the router alone and its three cascades, each with steps and operating points
